memories.content: The user renewed their local library membership in October 2024.
On an evening walk, the user saw an unlit street and took a detour along a main road.
On a day the user chose a well-lit pedestrian route, the walk took 12 minutes longer than usual.
On a day the user sat by the library window, they heard vehicle noise with every page they read.
On the next visit, the user sat farther inside and did not move for an hour.
The user wrote the due date of a borrowed book on paper and then lost the paper.
After entering the due date on their phone, the user saw a reminder the day before and put the book in their bag.
Library staff expect a person requesting a replacement membership card to bring identity-verification material.
Check recent lighting and pedestrian conditions before proposing an evening walking route.
The local agent can compare past reasons for detours but cannot directly observe current lighting and pedestrian conditions.
The user stores prepared meals on the second shelf of the freezer.
The user went to the market without a shopping list and bought onions that were already at home.
On a day the user shopped after checking a refrigerator photo, they did not make a duplicate purchase.
On a day the user made a spicy stew, they left part of one bowl uneaten.
The next time the user cooked it, they used half as much chili powder and finished the meal.
When cooking with their younger brother, the user assigned the cooking sequence only verbally and they did the same task twice.
The next time, the user and their younger brother split ingredient preparation and heat control and finished the meal 20 minutes earlier.
When cooking together, the user's younger brother prefers to divide the cooking and dishwashing roles in advance.
The local agent can compare responses across several meals, but it cannot conclude from one unfinished food item that the user dislikes that ingredient.
The condition of frozen prepared food may vary with its packaging and storage duration.

analysis.overview: The frames cover separate areas of the user’s life: library use and evening-route safety in the reference frame, and food storage, shopping, cooking, and meal coordination in the compared frame. No claims govern the same operational decision, so no cross-frame alignment or disagreement is established.
